scope: Solution architecture and impact analysis only; this record does not approve product scope, implementation, public release, or production deployment.

blockingDecisions: First supported platform and supported OS versions
Bounded MVP and explicitly deferred capabilities
Product differentiation and meaning of all devices
Open-source license, governance, security reporting, release ownership, and signing responsibility

architectureDecisions.decision: Use a shared, UI-independent download domain and transfer service with thin platform adapters. Do not select the desktop UI technology or first platform until the human product decision is recorded.

alternatives.name: Shared core with native UI per platform
advantages: One implementation of download state and integrity rules
alternatives.fit: Preferred if native means platform-native controls and the maintenance budget supports separate UIs

alternatives.name: Shared core with cross-platform desktop UI
tradeoffs: Native fidelity, binary size, resource use, and accessibility require framework-specific proof
alternatives.fit: Preferred if native means installable desktop applications rather than platform-native controls

alternatives.name: Independent application per operating system
tradeoffs: Highest implementation and long-term maintenance cost
alternatives.fit: Rejected unless evidence shows shared foundations cannot satisfy platform requirements

consequences: All UI, browser, CLI, and operating-system adapters consume the same state-transition and transfer policies.
Adapters may translate platform events but may not redefine pause, resume, retry, cancellation, destination conflict, or recovery rules.

architectureDecisions.decision: Model a download as a durable state machine owned by the shared domain service; persist metadata atomically and write content to a partial file before verified finalization.
requiredTransitions: active|paused|interrupted -> interrupted on application shutdown or restart recovery
invariants: Completed is recorded only after content finalization succeeds.
A partial file is never presented as completed.
Resume uses a validated server range response and matching remote identity; otherwise restart is explicit to the user.
Destination conflicts are resolved by an approved overwrite, rename, or cancel policy before transfer finalization.
Cancellation semantics for retaining or deleting partial data must be product-approved and user-visible.

persistenceOptions.name: Embedded transactional database
persistenceOptions.tradeoff: Strong atomic metadata transitions; introduces schema migration and recovery obligations

persistenceOptions.name: Atomic local manifest files
persistenceOptions.tradeoff: Small dependency surface; concurrency and corruption recovery are harder

architectureDecisions.selection: undecided pending workload, recovery, and platform evidence

architectureDecisions.decision: Treat browser capture as an optional adapter outside the transfer core and exclude it from the architecture baseline until the MVP boundary and supported browsers are approved.
constraints: Use authenticated, versioned local messaging with explicit user consent.
Validate URL schemes, message shape, origin context, redirects, and credential handling.
Never expose unrestricted filesystem or process capabilities to browser messages.

architectureDecisions.decision: Do not implement automatic updates or publish source or binaries until license, dependency policy, governance, vulnerability reporting, artifact ownership, signing, and rollback are approved.

alternatives.name: Platform stores or repositories
alternatives.tradeoff: Established trust channels but platform-specific review and policy constraints

alternatives.name: Project-hosted signed updates
alternatives.tradeoff: Consistent ownership but creates signing-key, update-service, rollback, and availability obligations

alternatives.name: Manual signed releases
alternatives.tradeoff: Smallest initial attack surface but slower security-update adoption

capabilityBoundary.capability: Progress, pause, resume, cancel, retry, completion, file location, and restart recovery

capabilityBoundary.status: undecided; must be absent by default or minimized, transparent, and consent-based

systemImpacts.impact: URLs, credentials, partial files, browser messages, logs, and update artifacts cross trust boundaries; threat modeling and sensitive-log tests are required before distribution.
Network loss, termination, disk exhaustion, destination conflicts, and servers without valid range support require executable recovery and integrity scenarios.
Concurrency must be bounded and platform budgets established for UI latency, CPU, memory, disk, and network use.
Core controls and asynchronous state changes require keyboard operation, visible focus, meaningful labels, and platform assistive-technology runtime tests.
Durable recovery requires atomic metadata persistence; the persistence technology and migration policy remain undecided.
Each platform requires reproducible packaging, artifact provenance, signing, update, and rollback ownership before binary release.
No analytics dependency is justified for the baseline; any telemetry requires a separate approved privacy specification.
No implementation impact is justified in the bounded desktop architecture; these areas are deferred unless human-approved scope changes.

implementationNotes: This workstream creates no application code and makes no implementation-readiness claim.
Downstream adapters must call the shared download domain and transfer service instead of duplicating business rules.
User-visible flows require real DOM, browser, integration, or equivalent desktop runtime evidence.
Only local, test, and staging are declared; production activity requires separate human approval.
knownRisks: Architecture selection is blocked by missing human product and platform decisions and missing discovery evidence.
Native has not been operationally defined, so choosing a UI framework now could conflict with product intent.
Range support and remote identity validation vary by server; incorrect resume logic can corrupt files.
Platform signing, notarization or reputation, updater security, and release ownership are unresolved.
Accessibility and resource-consumption claims require runtime measurement on every approved platform.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
